revision_history.note: [round2-blocking-findings-2026-09-02] ROUND 2 NOTE: supersedes the 4b93245 revision after the pre-landing reviewer's ROUND 2 returned 3 blocking findings, each REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION before it was fixed. (1) io_loop.rs:228 'the protocol-failure exception still leaks committed writes'. REPRODUCED over real sockets through the real server adapter: a peer completes the handshake, then sends ONE chunk carrying a masked close frame followed by a masked text frame. ConnectionCore::handle processes the close (COMMITTING the Q19 echo write) and then fails the text frame on the Closing state gate, all inside the same call; finish_poll returned that fatal Failure WITHOUT calling next_output, and the adapter halted at it by contract. The probe read 'peer received 0 post-handshake bytes ... dropped_frames=0 dropped_bytes=0' - the close reply the peer was waiting for was abandoned with nothing counted. The reviewer's named case, a SERVER HANDSHAKE REJECTION (handle_handshake_bytes queues the HTTP error head, then returns java_invalid_data), reached the peer before the fix only by ACCIDENT: drive_until_open ignored StepOutput::Failure from its inbound pump, so the run kept polling and eventually drained the head - and then burned its whole poll budget, reporting BudgetExhausted instead of the protocol failure (probe read: 'peer received 26 bytes HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found', 'outcome=BudgetExhausted polls=201'). FIX, at the seam rather than the adapter: ConnectionDriver::finish_poll now LATCHES a supplied fatal failure (pending_failure) and runs the ordinary output order, and next_output surfaces it only after the committed write stream has drained; the latch also counts as pending output, so no further input is applied while it is outstanding and the FIRST failure is the one delivered. DriverOutput::Failure is therefore ordered strictly AFTER every write the core had committed, including the write the failing step itself committed. The adapter now also HONORS the failure everywhere it can arrive - the drive_until_open inbound pump, both write-progress acknowledgements, and both EOF pumps previously discarded it. EXCEPTION NARROWED, NOT REMOVED: the protocol-failure arms still do not pump Shutdown, but what that exception now covers is exactly 'a connection whose driver has already handed over every committed write', and the residue is empty by the ordering rather than by assumption. Discrimination read: with finish_poll restored to returning the Failure directly, the three new loopback regressions fail at the PEER - rejection head left: [] right: the 26-byte 404; close echo left: [] right: [136, 2, 3, 232]; undeliverable-head accounting left: (0, 0) right: (1, 26) - and both new driver_contract pins fail with 'got Failure(JavaInvalidData)'. (2) mapping.go:739 'the US-017 exact linkage omits DroppedWrites, DriverOutput::WritesDropped and CommandRefusalReason::ReceiverDropped'. REPRODUCED: in an isolated copy of the derivation inputs, deleting `pub struct DroppedWrites` produced only a generic LINKAGE_DAG_DRIFTED (a co-located symbol's file digest), the SANCTIONED regeneration then returned err=<nil>, and the re-verify read [] - the removal was laundered into a freshly 'verified' artifact. FIX: all three symbols have catalog specifications and US-017 'implements' edges, and the artifacts were regenerated with LINKAGE_REGENERATE=1 (exit 0) and re-verified without the flag (exit 0). Deletion-sensitive polarity is committed as internal/linkage TestDeletingAnAC2TypedSymbolFailsTheLinkageGate: each declaration is actually removed and BOTH Verify and WriteArtifacts must refuse by name. Post-fix probe reads LINKAGE_DERIVATION_FAILED and a regeneration error, both naming ws_driver::DroppedWrites. (3) results.json:15 'the PASS artifact still names the 3df6371 source and harness blobs'. REPRODUCED by the new gate before anything was corrected: 'target.source records git_blob 2dab104... for rust/ws-driver/src/lib.rs, but the committed tree hashes to b0bea8c...' and 'target.harness records git_blob 8d51594... but the committed tree hashes to 76aeb3c...'. Both are corrected here, and the class is now detectable rather than reviewed: internal/formalplan.ValidateConcurrencyResults recomputes every file-naming binding in this document - the two target blobs (git's own blob-object construction, pinned against git's ids), the preregistered plan sha256, every minimized_reproduction, and all seven pinned minimized artifacts - and its polarity test makes each one stale in turn, from BOTH sides (the recorded id edited, and the named file edited), reading the typed refusal each time. SWEEP COUNTERS ARE UNCHANGED, re-executed and read identical: 79,920 schedules, 315,070 branches, 18,755 distinct trace digests, 56,777/23,143 closed/halted, 37,813 reports / 134,430 bytes / 4,172 partial-front, max_dropped_frames 1, 79,920 receiver-drop refusals, fatal sweep 56,189 / 198,037 with per-budget 7,572/23,072/13,985/11,560, deferred_output_pending 41,773. The failure latch is a no-op whenever nothing is committed - next_output takes it on the same poll that set it - and no schedule in this alphabet reaches a fatal step with a committed write outstanding, which is exactly why the sweep cannot witness the guarantee and why it is pinned at the unit and adapter level instead (see limitations). The seven pinned minimized artifacts and both regression seeds are byte-identical and were not refrozen. Prior revision notes (session 01a04960 round 1, session 01a0464f round 2, and BLOCKING-1/2 of session 01a04626 with the stale preregistered_plan.sha256 correction) remain in force. (revision round2-blocking-findings-2026-09-02, SUPERSEDED)

[round3-blocking-finding-2026-09-02] ROUND 3 (pre-landing review, this revision) returned ONE blocking finding, and it was REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION BEFORE ANY FIX WAS WRITTEN. THE FINDING: internal/formalplan/concurrency_results_test.go did not provide the discrimination the round-2 note below claimed for it. That claim - that the polarity test makes each binding stale in turn from BOTH sides - held for the two target blobs and for one of the seven retention seeds, and was FALSE for everything else: neither minimized_reproduction binding was ever mutated, no half path/sha256 binding was ever constructed, and target.harness, the preregistered plan and six of the seven retention seeds had only one side exercised. Both deletions were run and read green first; that is the finding, demonstrated. FIX: the polarity coverage is no longer a hand-maintained list, because a hand-maintained list is what went stale. TestEveryResultsBindingIsRefusedFromBothSides enumerates the bindings FROM THIS DOCUMENT (crEnumerateBindings, pinned at 12 by crBindingCount so the loop cannot silently empty, and rejecting any half-recorded binding it finds) and makes every one stale from the RECORDED side (the digest text edited in place, with anchor uniqueness enforced so a probe cannot read the right refusal for the wrong binding) and from the NAMED-FILE side (the file itself edited), reading the typed refusal each time; the isolated tree it mutates is built from that same enumeration, so the fixture cannot drift from what the gate reads. TestAHalfMinimizedReproductionBindingIsRefused constructs a path-without-sha256 and a sha256-without-path for BOTH recorded minimized_reproduction bindings. TestAnAbsentMinimizedReproductionStaysLegitimate pins the opposite polarity of the same loop: the 8 defects that legitimately record no reproduction must NOT be refused. TestAnUnusableResultsDocumentIsRefused closes the three intake arms this round own adversarial pass found uncovered (artifact absent, artifact over the 1 MiB bound, artifact unparseable). POST-FIX DISCRIMINATION READ: with the minimized-reproduction loop deleted, 8 subtests fail and name both bindings; with only the incomplete-binding refusal deleted, 4 fail, and their text shows exactly the degradation that had made the branch invisible - a path-without-digest falls through to RESULTS_ARTIFACT_DIGEST_STALE and a digest-without-path to RESULTS_TARGET_PATH_MISSING, so demanding the typed RESULTS_ARTIFACT_BINDING_INCOMPLETE is what makes the deletion fail. THE BOTH-SIDES CLAIM NOW STANDS AS WRITTEN, and it was settled by enumerating the bindings in code rather than by reading the sentence: this document declares 12 file-naming bindings - target.source, target.harness, preregistered_plan, defects_found_and_fixed[0] and [4] minimized_reproduction, and retention.minimized_artifacts[0] through [6] - and each of the 12 has both polarity cases, generated by the same enumeration the gate walks, so a binding added later cannot ship without them. NOT re-run: the native-thread stress and the fuzz campaigns. NOT refrozen: the seven pinned minimized artifacts and both regression seeds, which remain byte-identical. The only regeneration was the SANCTIONED linkage refreeze that editing this file requires (LINKAGE_REGENERATE=1, exit 0; re-verified without the flag, exit 0), which changed exactly one line, the evidence-dag sha256 of this document. bounds.program_shape: producer A [send_text, send_binary]; producer B [send_ping, send_close]; transport-read [inbound-ping, inbound-close, transport-eof]; transport-write [write-partial, write-all, write-all]; adapter-control [wake, shutdown]

scenario_shapes.name: abnormal-teardown
scenario_shapes.program_shape: producer A [send_text, send_binary]; producer B [send_ping, send_close]; transport-read [inbound-ping, inbound-close, transport-eof]; transport-write [write-partial, write-all, write-all]; adapter-control [wake, shutdown]
scenario_shapes.models: the exceptional path: the embedding application tearing down, or the write side failing, while the peer is also closing. The adapter Shutdowns AND the read side reaches EOF, so the connection is terminated twice.
scenario_shapes.why_explored: the original and, until owner decision us017-exploration-program-set-owner-decision-2026-08-28 (sha 86793909), the ONLY program set. With the driver's EOF coalescing fixed, every schedule here halts on the second scored termination, which is correct and is why a second scenario is required to cover the normal lifecycle at all.

scenario_shapes.name: clean-finish
scenario_shapes.program_shape: producer A [send_text]; producer B [send_close]; transport-read [inbound-close, transport-eof]; transport-write [write-all, write-all]; adapter-control [wake]
scenario_shapes.models: the ordinary WebSocket close lifecycle: the application sends a message and initiates close, the peer's close frame arrives, the committed frames flush, and the read side reaches EOF exactly ONCE. A healthy adapter never calls Shutdown on this path - Shutdown means the adapter can provide no further transport service and belongs to abnormal teardown. The ws-testee io_loop drives exactly this shape.
scenario_shapes.why_explored: owner decision us017-exploration-program-set-owner-decision-2026-08-28 (sha 86793909). The previous single-scenario set modelled ONLY the abnormal double-termination path, so the normal lifecycle every real deployment spends its life in was never actually explored - its apparent coverage came from two terminations being silently merged into one by the driver's EOF coalescing defect. Its clean route is NARROW: 49 of its 1260 schedules reach a clean terminal and they carry 18 distinct semantic traces, which is why scenario clean-finish-inbound-ping exists beside it rather than instead of it.

scenario_shapes.name: clean-finish-inbound-ping
scenario_shapes.program_shape: producer A [send_text]; producer B [send_close]; transport-read [inbound-ping, inbound-close, transport-eof]; transport-write [write-all, write-all]; adapter-control [wake, wake]
scenario_shapes.models: the ordinary WebSocket close lifecycle with a keepalive ping still in flight: the application sends a message and initiates close, the peer's ping arrives ahead of its close frame because peers ping on an idle timer that does not know a close is coming, the committed frames flush, and the read side reaches EOF exactly ONCE. Two owner turns, because an adapter polls repeatedly. No Shutdown, for the reason scenario clean-finish gives.
scenario_shapes.why_explored: the post-failure landing review's finding 1 (drafts/self-review/post-failure-landing-review.md). Scenario clean-finish reaches a clean terminal in 49 of its 1260 schedules and those 49 runs carry only 18 distinct semantic traces, so the four properties that hold ONLY on the clean route were exercised against eighteen behaviours in a single scenario. Lengthening the READ program rather than the producer programs is what buys clean breadth, because it gives the producers somewhere to be scheduled that is not a state violation. Measured on this scenario alone: 1127 clean-terminal runs carrying 385 distinct traces.

adapter_model: the interpreter drives the public driver boundary exactly as the real adapter does: a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure HALTS the run at that instant (ws-testee io_loop maps it to LoopOutcome::ProtocolFailure and stops), so no schedule action, drain poll, or quiescence poll follows a Failure; Terminal-after-Failure is impossible by construction and additionally asserted. WHY THAT HALT IS SAFE (round-2 re-review, io_loop.rs:228): halting is only sound because DriverOutput::Failure is ordered strictly AFTER the committed write stream, so an adapter that stops there has already been offered every byte the core committed - including the bytes the failing step itself committed. Before that ordering existed the same halt abandoned a committed write at the peer with nothing counted, which this model would not have caught: the boundary computes what the transport OWED only on Action::Shutdown, so a run that halts without a shutdown records owed=0 by construction. The ordering guarantee is therefore evidenced by driver_contract.rs and by ws-testee loopback tests over real sockets, NOT by this sweep

terminal_disposition_model: every full schedule ends in one of two typed dispositions: the clean Terminal from the absorbing Closed state (1176 runs, spread over the clean-finish and clean-finish-inbound-ping scenarios and carrying 403 distinct semantic traces between them, which is the count that says how much of the clean route is actually covered); or the halt at the first surfaced fatal Failure (90984 runs, exactly one surfaced failure each), the poisoned core retaining its final state under the oracle's partial-execution semantics, which is why the halt is itself a terminal disposition. The two are ORDERED, not mutually exclusive: a converged connection refuses work still pushed at it rather than absorbing it, so a run may take its one clean Terminal and only then reach a fatal, which halted_terminals runs do. No terminal is ever recorded after a failure, and that ordering - not exclusivity - is what the harness asserts against the trace. Both classes reconcile every accepted command exactly once on the clean route and at most once on the halted one.

defects_found_and_fixed.finding_verbatim: A pending `WritesDropped` disposition is suppressed by a fatal `Failure`, after which the adapter halts, leaving a reachable committed write silently unreported.
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::finish_poll returns a supplied fatal TypedProtocolFailure WITHOUT calling next_output, so a DroppedWrites report set moments earlier by the Shutdown arm was never surfaced. The latched EOF is applied inside that same shutdown poll, and it fails fatally with ActionLimitExceeded once the action budget is spent, so the whole observable output of the run became a single Failure and the committed frame vanished. A faithful adapter halts at its first Failure, so anything queued behind it is unreachable by construction.
defects_found_and_fixed.ac_reading: AC2 lists adapter shutdown in the same typed-behaviour clause as every other terminal disposition and carves out no exception for fatal termination; 'cannot leak' is unconditional, so the report is owed on the fatal route exactly as on the clean one.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: has_pending_output now counts an undelivered DroppedWrites report alongside an offered write, so the driver applies NO input while one is outstanding. A fatal failure can only be produced by APPLYING an input, so none can exist to suppress the report. Structural, not an ordering rule: the report is surfaced strictly before any failure can be generated. Schedules with nothing committed pending are bit-for-bit unaffected, because the report is only set when frames > 0.

max_dropped_frames_in_one_report is 1 across all 92160 schedules of THIS sweep, which runs under the explicit AutoResponsePolicy::Disabled configuration. CORRECTION (pre-landing review finding 1, session 01a04960): the previous text called that value structural, and it is not. Under the DEFAULT AutoResponsePolicy::PongInboundPing an automatic pong is injected while a semantic event is being RETURNED, so it never passes through the offered-write gate; it sits in the core's write queue while the next poll applies a producer command on top of it, and the shutdown that follows reports frames=2,bytes=12. That was reproduced by execution before this correction was written and is now pinned by driver_contract.rs::a_shutdown_report_accounts_for_every_committed_frame_not_just_the_offered_one. The plural accumulation in abort_pending_writes is therefore an EXERCISED path under the shipped default, and only the report COUNT (one per run) is a bounded property; the frame count is not.

a fatal Failure halt with NO shutdown ever polled leaves committed writes with the driver rather than abandoned by it, so no dropped-write report is owed there; the ws-testee io_loop deliberately does not pump Shutdown on its protocol-failure path. CORRECTED (round-2 re-review, session 01a04960): the previous text asserted that stance was safe, and it was not. A fatal core step can COMMIT a wire write and FAIL in the same call - a server handshake rejection queues its HTTP error head before returning java_invalid_data, and a chunk carrying an inbound close followed by a data frame queues the Q19 echo before failing the state gate - and finish_poll surfaced that Failure without draining, so the halt abandoned a committed write AT THE PEER with dropped_frames=0. Reproduced over real sockets before it was fixed. DriverOutput::Failure is now ordered strictly after the committed write stream, so the no-shutdown exit covers only connections that have already handed over everything committed; the exception is narrowed to that, not removed. This sweep does NOT witness the guarantee: no schedule in the 12-action alphabet reaches a fatal step with a committed write outstanding, so an owed-at-halt assertion here would be vacuous. It is pinned instead by driver_contract.rs::a_fatal_input_that_commits_a_write_offers_the_write_before_the_failure, driver_contract.rs::an_undrained_committed_write_is_reported_when_the_failing_run_shuts_down, and three ws-testee loopback tests that read what the PEER receives (a_rejected_server_handshake_delivers_its_committed_error_head_before_failing, a_protocol_failure_after_a_committed_close_echo_still_delivers_the_echo, a_protocol_failure_whose_committed_write_cannot_be_delivered_is_accounted)

CARRIED FORWARD, out of scope for this revision and deliberately NOT fixed here (found while fixing round 2, restated so it is not lost): both write-progress acknowledgement arms in rust/ws-testee/src/io_loop.rs - the connected pump and the drive_until_open handshake pump - inspect the acknowledgement only for StepOutput::Failure and DISCARD every other output it carries. ConnectionDriver::next_output pops a semantic event from the core queue when it returns one, so an acknowledgement that yields Event(InputChunk { bytes: 8 }) consumes that event and drops it: the adapter never calls record_event for it and never offers it to the auto-response policy, so it is missing from the ConnectionReport and, under the default PongInboundPing policy, a ping arriving that way would draw no pong. A StepOutput::Terminal arriving on an acknowledgement is lost the same way, and the delivery is exactly-once. WritesDropped is NOT affected - pump accounts it before the arm sees it. This changes adapter-observable behaviour and could touch the Autobahn and cross-peer legs, so it needs its own scoped pass rather than a correction folded into a polarity round; no claim in this document rests on it.

CLEAN-ROUTE COVERAGE CEILING: the clean-terminal route is the thinner half of this exploration, and the RUN count overstates it. Of 92160 explored schedules, 1176 reach a clean terminal and 90984 halt at the first surfaced fatal failure. Those clean-terminal runs carry 403 distinct semantic traces, against 4587 for the space as a whole, so the four properties that hold ONLY on the clean route - convergence under weak fairness, the exactly-once reconciliation of every accepted command, post-terminal quiescence, and no write bypass - are exercised against 403 behaviours, not against the run count. They are reached in 2 of the 3 scenarios: abnormal-teardown contributes none, correctly, because with the EOF coalescing defect fixed every schedule there halts on its second scored termination. WHAT THIS CEILING FORBIDS: no claim about this suite's clean-close concurrency coverage may be strengthened on the schedule count. The schedule count is dominated by abnormal-teardown, whose schedules all end in a halt, and a defect that manifests only in a trace masked by an early refusal-halt is not explored by any of them. WHY IT IS NOT WIDER: a clean finish requires every producer enqueue to land before the peer's close, so the clean fraction of any freely-interleaved scenario falls as the programs lengthen; and the preregistered plan caps the enumeration at bounds.schedule_count_max, which this revision did not edit. Widening the clean route further means another scenario within that cap, not a larger one.
